Here's a proof of is_closest, no sorry, standard axioms only:

import Mathlib

def closest_mult (j V : ℕ) : ℕ := ((V + j / 2) / j) * j

lemma is_multiple {j V : ℕ} : j ∣ closest_mult j V := by
  unfold closest_mult
  apply dvd_mul_left

lemma is_closest {j V x : ℕ} (h : j ∣ x) : Nat.dist (closest_mult j V) V ≤ Nat.dist x V := by
  by_contra hcontr;
  -- Let $q = (V + j / 2) / j$ and $r = (V + j / 2) % j$.
  set q := (V + j / 2) / j
  set r := (V + j / 2) % j
  have hq : j * q = closest_mult j V := by
    exact Nat.mul_comm _ _
  have hr : r < j := by
    apply Nat.mod_lt;
    cases j <;> simp_all +decide [ closest_mult ];
  -- From definition of $q$ and $r$, we have $j * q + r = V + j /  �2�$.
  have h_div : j * q + r = V + j / 2 := by
    rw [ Nat.div_add_mod ];
  -- Since $j$ divides $ �x�$, there exists some integer $k$ such that $x = j * k$.
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, x = j * k := h;
  rcases lt_trichotomy k q with hk | rfl | hk <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.dist ];
  · zify at *;
    cases le_total ( j * k ) V <;> cases le_total ( closest_mult j V ) V <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.cast_sub ] <;> nlinarith [ Nat.div_mul_le_self j 2 ] ;
  · zify at *;
    cases le_total ( j * k ) V <;> cases le_total ( closest_mult j V ) V <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.cast_sub ];
    · nlinarith [ Nat.div_mul_le_self ( j / 2 ) 2, Nat.div_add_mod j 2, Nat.mod_lt j two_pos ];
    · nlinarith [ Nat.div_add_mod ( V + j / 2 ) j, Nat.mod_lt ( V + j / 2 ) ( by linarith : 0 < j ), Nat.div_mul_le_self ( V + j / 2 ) j ];
    · nlinarith [ Nat.div_add_mod ( V + j / 2 ) j, Nat.mod_lt ( V + j / 2 ) ( by linarith : 0 < j ), Nat.div_mul_le_self ( V + j / 2 ) j, Nat.div_add_mod j 2, Nat.mod_lt j two_pos ];
    · nlinarith [ Nat.div_add_mod ( V + j / 2 ) j, Nat.mod_lt ( V + j / 2 ) ( Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by aesop_cat : j ≠ 0 ) ) ]

Strategy: contradiction on the dist inequality, case split on k vs q via lt_trichotomy, lift to ℤ with zify, then nlinarith closes each branch using the division/modulus bounds.

Mine goes this way (and is more noobish):

import Mathlib

def closest_mult (j V : ℕ) : ℕ := ((V + j / 2) / j) * j

lemma is_multiple (j V : ℕ) : j ∣ (closest_mult j V) := by
  unfold closest_mult
  apply dvd_mul_left

lemma thm₀ (j V : ℕ) (h : j ≠ 0): closest_mult j (V + j) = closest_mult j V + j := by
  unfold closest_mult
  rw [show V + j + j / 2 = V + j / 2 + j by ring, Nat.add_div_right _ (by grind)]
  grind

lemma thm₁ {j V x : ℕ} (h : j ∣ x) (h₀ : V + j / 2 < j) :
    Nat.dist (closest_mult j V) V ≤ Nat.dist x V := by
  unfold closest_mult
  rw [Nat.div_mul_self_eq_mod_sub_self, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h₀, tsub_self, Nat.dist_zero_left,
    Nat.dist]
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := h
  cases d <;> grind

lemma thm₂ {j V x : ℕ} (h : j ∣ x) (h₀ : j ≤ V + j / 2) (h₁ : V < j) :
    Nat.dist (closest_mult j V) V ≤ Nat.dist x V := by
  unfold closest_mult
  have h₂ : V + j / 2 - j < j := by grind
  rw [Nat.div_mul_self_eq_mod_sub_self, Nat.mod_eq_sub_mod h₀, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h₂,
    Nat.dist, Nat.dist]
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := h
  cases d <;> grind

lemma is_closest (j V x : ℕ) (h : j ∣ x) : Nat.dist (closest_mult j V) V ≤ Nat.dist x V := by
  by_cases h₀ : j = 0
  · grind [closest_mult, Nat.dist, zero_dvd_iff]
  revert x h; induction V using Nat.strong_induction_on; rename_i V ih; intros x h
  by_cases h₁ : V < j
  · by_cases h₂ : V + j / 2 < j
    . exact thm₁ h h₂
    · exact thm₂ h (by grind) h₁
  · rw [show V = (V - j) + j by grind, thm₀ _ _ h₀, Nat.dist_add_add_right]
    have h₂ := ih (V - j) (by grind) (x - j) (by rw [Nat.dvd_sub_self_right]; grind)
    by_cases h₃ : x = 0
    · grind [zero_tsub, Nat.dist_zero_left]
    · have h₄ : j ≤ x := (Nat.le_iff_ne_zero_of_dvd (by grind) h).mpr h₃
      rwa [show x = x - j + j by grind, Nat.dist_add_add_right]
